speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: We shall continue consideration of item 241.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I see an item here for 28 air traffic control assistants, listed in the civil staff. Does that mean that civilians

Supply-National Defence have replaced service personnel in this employment, or does this represent a new category of employment?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The Royal Canadian Air Force took over from the Department of Transport a number of air stations. At the present time there are 28 air traffic control assistants located at seven air traffic control centres across Canada, namely at Saint John, New Brunswick, Moncton, Dorval, Toronto, Winnipeg, Edmonton and Vancouver. Their job is to pass on flight plan information concerning all aircraft in their area to the air defence control centre, so that particular flights may be identified. This is part of the air defence of North America.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I see that under the civil staff there appears to be an appreciable increase in the number of clerks and stenographers, as well as diesel power plant operators. Are these additional employees, or are they civilian personnel who are replacing service personnel in certain categories of employment?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The diesel engine operators are stationary engineers at radar stations where power plants are located, and the others mentioned by the hon. member represent an endeavour to use civilian rather than service personnel wherever possible.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I have mentioned a considerable increase in the number of clerks and stenographers in the civil staff. It seems to me there has been a considerable increase in the number of service stenographers employed by the air force in the last year, due to the fact that women are again being recruited in that force. Would the minister give us some indication of the over-all increase in the number of stenographic employees?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The increase in stenographic employees is related to the increase in the activities of the R.C.A.F. generally. The number of man-years is one way of measuring it. In the year 1952-53 the number of man-years in the R.C.A.F., as related to this point, was 37,073, while in 1953-54 it is estimated the number will be 44,309. The civilian increase is related to that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
Last year an item appeared in the estimates for the employment of chauffeurs in Brussels and Moscow. No doubt this was in connection with air attaches. This year the item does not appear.
I presume these chauffeurs are now service personnel; is that the explanation?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
The service personnel in Brussels have been -Changed so there is no longer an air attache there. In Moscow it has to be a serviceman.
(Mr. MacLean (Queens).]

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Then under the heading of major procurement of equipment I find an item for aircraft and engines, which has been increased from $223,545,000 to $420,232,600. What does that increase represent? Then I see a separate item for armament equipment, and another item for signal and wireless equipment. Does this include airborne equipment, or is the cost of airborne armament included with aircraft and engines? Does the sub-item of armament equipment include airborne as well as ground equipment?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
The first item of $420,232,600 covers aircraft of all types, and everything that goes into aircraft. The major components are, for the Sabre, $65 million; for the CF-100, $77 million; for the C-119 Packets, $3 million; for the de Havilland Comet, $700,000; for the Otter, $660,000. Then there is an item for customs, excise, sales tax, etc. of $9,810,000 and an item for the Lockheed trainer, which is the T-33, of $1,703,000. The figures I have given relate to the total program, and the amount of that total program of $1,146,640,000 which we expect to spend in 1953-54 is $420,232,600.
The second item to which the hon. member referred is armament. The estimate for cash required is $4,515,000. That includes ground armament, airborne gun and rocketfiring and sighting equipment, guided missile equipment, test and handling equipment, passive defence equipment, freight, express, customs and excise.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I was a little surprised to have the minister give a breakdown of the $420 million as between the amount for Sabres, the amount for CF-lOO's and so forth in view of the fact that when I tried to get that information last year in the defence expenditure committee with respect to the item of $687 million which had been spent on aircraft up to that time I was refused the information on the grounds of security. But as the minister has now given a breakdown as far as the $420 million is concerned, I wonder if he would be prepared to give one with respect to the item of $687 million which we had up to this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I did not give a breakdown of the expenditures involved in the $420,232,600. I gave the division with respect to the total program, which I do not think would have any security attached to it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I understood the minister was giving a breakdown of the $420 million. He gave so much for Sabres, so much for CF-lOO's, so much for T-33's and so on. What does that refer to if it does not refer to the $420 million?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The balance of the authorized program totalling $1,146,640,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I am not quite clear as to what the breakdown the minister gave referred to unless it had reference to the $420 million. Is that what it referred to?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I am afraid not. I gave the figures with regard to the total program, but not the amount of cash that would be spent this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I certainly do not think the figures the minister gave referred to the total program which includes this $420 million up to January 1 of last year, I think it was. There is over a billion there alone, and the figures he gave certainly do not add up to anything like that. I did not put them down, but having kept rough track of them I would say that they do not even add up to $420 million.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The figures are made up of a carryover from the program of $981,022,000, that has already been entered upon and committed, and the new program of $165,618,000, or a total of $1,146,640,000, of which $726,407,400 is to be liquidated in future years.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: We seem to be talking at cross purposes. What exactly was the breakdown that the minister gave? He mentioned $65 million for Sabres and $3 million for C-119's. I have forgotten what the other figures were.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The items I mentioned plus some others that are similar total $165,618,000, which is the new program in addition to that already put before parliament and in respect of which we have commitment authority.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: What relation do these figures have to the $420 million? Are they included in it or are they in addition to it?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The $420 million that I mentioned will be used to finance the carryover, plus new program, less commitments to be liquidated in future years which total $726,407,400. The details I gave, including the $65 million odd for Sabres and $77 million for Canucks, are the new program.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: If I understand this properly, the $165 million is all of the new program which is included in the $420 million. The $420 million is the previous commitments from last year and the year before but which is going to be spent this year, less the amount that the minister indicated.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
Less the amount that will be spent in future years; that is right.
Supply-National Defence

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Less the amount to be spent in future years. In other words, this consists of money commitments which were made in past years, plus the $165 million which is a new commitment to be spent this year, plus commitments for future years.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
Less commitments for future
years.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The $420 million includes commitments for future years too, does it not?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Solicitor General of Canada
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is the cash element to be spent for this present fiscal year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: If that is the cash element, then the $420 million minus the $165 million, which would be approximately $260 million, represents cash expenditures on commitments from past years.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is right-to be made this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: There are no commitments for future years included in this at all?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Not in the whole $420 million.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: We have a breakdown of $165 million out of the $420 million. Can we get a similar breakdown for the remaining $260 million odd?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: We have not got a breakdown of that. The way in which I put the figures was that we have a commitment authority carryover of $981,022,000 and a new program of $165,618,000, or a total of $1,146,640,000, from which $726,407,400 is to be subtracted because it is to be liquidated in future years. The difference is the cash required for this year of $420,232,600, of which $165,618,000 is covered by the details I gave.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: As I understand the picture now, there is a carry-over of $981 million included in which is $260 million odd which is included in this item, for which cash is going to be put out this year, and of which we have not had a breakdown.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: And the remainder, which would be about $720 million, has still not been committed. Is that correct?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: It is committed but it will not have to be met in 1953-54.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: May I put it this way. Of this $981 million there is a further amount of approximately $720 million which will not be spent this year and which has not been spent up to date.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
That is right.
4054	HOUSE OF
Supply-National Defence

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: But it has all been committed?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: For this total amount which has been committed but not spent can the minister give us any breakdown-although I am not insisting-of how it is to be spent?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I think the same reasoning would apply here as applied in the defence expenditure committee.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: In view of the fact that we have had a breakdown of part of this $420 million which is actually to be spent this year, it would seem to me that we should be able to have a breakdown of the whole thing. I would think that as far as security is concerned the rule which applies in one place should apply in the other.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: A partial breakdown does not give you or anyone else anything, except as related to the amount we are seeking here in the total breakdown.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: It does if you give it year by year. The minister has given it this year and he will presumably give it in future years.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Is it desirable to give it?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I cannot see why not unless the minister is going to say in some future year that he will not give the breakdown for that year. If he is going to give the breakdown year by year, as he has for this year's operation, when the whole program is completed we will have the whole picture. Is there any difference between giving it for the whole program and giving it year by year until the whole program is completed? If there is some valid security reason perhaps we would be able to understand, but I cannot see it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Perhaps I was wrong in giving it a moment ago, but that does not justify us giving the whole thing which would enable one, by a simple process of division, to arrive at the total production of fighter aircraft, something that is not we believe in the public interest to give.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
May I ask the minister how much cash has actually been expended since the three-year program started? It is very difficult to keep track of these things, with these commitments, hold-overs and so on. As far as I can make out, $165 million of new expenditure is to be made this year and there is a $981 million carryover from money which was authorized by parliament in past years. In addition to the $981 million authorization or commitment or whatever you


wish to call it, how much has actually been expended as far as the three-year program is concerned?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The total amount expended for each service-

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I mean just for the air force.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: -on that major division is given in the white paper at pages 36 and 37.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Where on pages 36 and 37 would we relate this $981 million to the total amount voted and the total amount expended? That is the thing I do not see.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: What the hon. gentleman was asking a moment ago was the amount that had been spent during the past three years?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Well, that is included in the item on page 37: procurement of equipment.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Not for aircraft.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: It was aircraft I was asking about because I was trying to relate it to the total $981 million carryover and also to the total amount that had been voted.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I would be glad indeed to get for the hon. member the total expenditure on aircraft provided that we do not have to break it down into types. I will get it for the hon. member.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: May I ask a question? Have the CF-lOO's which are now being organized into squadrons at North Bay been equipped yet with electronic gun sights?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: They are being equipped with radar sights, yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I know they are to be equipped but they are not so equipped at the present time.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Well, they are.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: They are or they are not equipped?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: They are equipped.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: They are equipped with electronic gun sights now?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes. While this is a field which is pretty technical for me, as I understand it they are equipped now; and there are developments occurring which are resulting in their being equipped as they pome off the line with a subsequent development, the very latest thing.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
There is one other observation which I am forced to make. On April 14, at page 3811 of Hansard, the minister said

that the radar system would be largely completed in 1953. I know this is highly bound up by security, but that estimate is so far from the estimates that I have been given by other sources that I just wanted to ask the minister whether by any chance a mistake had been made in his estimates.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No, that is correct. As regards the Canadian part of the radar chain, as it is presently planned, we expect that it will be largely operational in 1953. A good number of the permanent stations are operational now.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Last year there was $223 million spent for aircraft and engines. Of that amount more than one-third was spent outside of Canada. From the returns I have here this year we plan to spend $420 million on the same item. How much of that will be spent outside of Canada?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is a matter for the Department of Defence Production. From the figures I have seen it will be very much less in proportion because for one thing we are producing the Orenda engine in quantity. It will go into the F-86E Sabre-it is going in now-and that will mean a very large additional element of each aircraft of that type will be produced in Canada.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: You expect the same ratio of purchases as last year would follow?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No, I think it would be very much less.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: You have no idea how much less?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: In that connection, I want to ask how much of our defence money has been spent in Britain up to date?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is in the white paper, in so far as it can be sorted out into the main end items, and it appears at page 34. During 1951-52 we have spent $9,962,000; in 1952-53, for ten months, $15,732,000, and that is largely for Centurion tanks. In addition to that we have spent considerable sums on components that have gone into these new ships.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I was given a figure of $100 million from the department up to the end of 1952. It seems to me it is a matter of very great importance having regard to the balance of payments between Britain and ourselves. I am wondering if the minister can hold out any hope that more can be done. I was told at one time that deliveries were slow, but later I was told that the
Supply-National Defence difficulty was clearing up. I wonder if the minister can say something about it, as I think it is a matter of great importance.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
My colleagues the Minister of Defence Production and the Minister of Finance are continuously directing their attention to this subject. We have had also, of course, a number of conversations with representatives of the British government and their department of defence, to see in what ways we could enlarge these expenditures. There are considerable difficulties in the way of getting delivery and also of having equipment of the types that we want. We are getting all the Centurions we can from Britain, but in the case of F-86E Sabres the flow is the other way.
We are exploring, for example, the possibility of acquiring or getting the right to make a new type of long-range aircraft for production about 1956-57.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I do not want to labour the point, but when we are having difficulty selling things from this country, such as cheese and things of that sort, I am wondering if the minister can assure us that it is a matter of constant effort on the part of those who are responsible for purchasing to have it in mind that, all other things being equal or nearly equal, we should purchase in Britain. We are trying all kinds of ways of adjusting the balance, and it seems to me that here is a way because we are here spending many hundreds of millions of dollars.
I would not disagree that there are difficulties; I know they exist. There is an old music hall maxim, however, which says "where there is a will there are three ways." If everyone has it in mind, it seems to me that a great deal could be done.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is right. This is the business of my colleague the Minister of Defence Production. I assure the hon. member he has this problem very much in the forefront of his mind, just as his officers have. They are doing everything possible in that direction.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Following the hon. member's remarks just now, I notice that according to a return I have here it would appear that we purchased last year aircraft engines and planes from Britain to the value of $22-5 million and from the United States to the value of $54 million. Is that correct?

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
The minister has said twice that the Minister of Defence Production is the minister dealing with that problem, together with the Minister of Finance; therefore I think we ought-
4056	HOUSE OF
Supply-National Defence Mr. Higgins: It is in the minister's estimates.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is the amount to be spent, and if you want to ask for any information concerning the purposes for which the money was spent, that is quite relevant. Information concerning where the contracts are being let is a matter, according to the minister's statement, that is left to the Minister of Defence Production.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: With deference, Mr. Chairman, this was a return of the house which is in Hansard of March 30, 1953 at page 3397. It shows the sum of $54 million having been spent for aircraft and engines in the United States, while $22-5 million was spent in Britain.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Was the return filed by the Minister of National Defence or the Minister of Defence Production?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Is it material who files it?

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: It is when we are studying the estimates. The estimates of the Minister of Defence Production will come later, and questions relating to his department should be asked at that time. It will be quite proper for the hon. member to ask the question then. I do not want to get involved in a long discussion on procedure.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: There is an item here, "aircraft engines". What other item would enable a member to ask a question except this item "aircraft engines" in the minister's estimates?

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: It seems to me that if the Minister of National Defence requisitioned the Minister of Defence Production to purchase aircraft engines, it would be for the Minister of Defence Production to inform the house as to where he let his contracts, whether it is in Britain or the United States. That is my view.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: May I point out that the Minister of National Defence asks the Minister of Defence Production to purchase aircraft, and he specifies the kind of aircraft or engines he wants. In other words he specifies whether it is a British engine or a United States engine. I think, therefore, it is proper to ask questions of this sort because the minister is the one who specifies the type of engine to be secured.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Defence Production; Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
With respect to the reference by the hon. member for St. John's East to the question and answer appearing on page 3397 of Hansard for March 30, 1953, about which he is now seeking to question the Minister of National Defence, I may say that the information does not relate to the procurement of aircraft engines for defence at all. [The Chairman.]

It is a statistical figure showing the number of airplanes and engines imported into Canada, and includes all sorts of commercial aircraft, engines and that sort of thing. It has no bearing upon defence expenditures in any way.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: May I point out that the Minister of National Defence, in his own white paper, sets out how much money has been spent in the United Kingdom and how much has been spent in the United States. Surely the hon. member for St. John's East is entitled to ask a question along that line. As I understood it, that was what he was doing.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: My remarks were made in the light of the reply which the minister gave. In any event the minister wants to take the floor.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
There is no doubt about the right of the hon. member for St. John's East to ask the question, but the question is whether I can answer it. None of the figures I have here will answer it. The Department of Defence Production have the figures and can give the answer. I suggest, as the chairman did, that is the department to which the hon. member should put his question.
I may say, in a general way, that during the year we bought some Bristol freighters, some Merlin engines and at the end of the year we bought two Comet aircraft. Apart from that I do not recall that we made any purchases of aircraft or their parts from Britain during the year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: It is correct to say that the Minister of National Defence does not actually keep a tabulation of the orders that he places?

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Well, why should he?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I ask the Minister of Defence Production to procure some equipment. He is the person who selects where the equipment is to be procured and keeps the figures on the contracts and so forth. We provide him in the end with the money.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Would it be fair to ask him to answer the question?

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
May I point out to you, Mr. Chairman, that as I see it, unless we were to do it under the first item of the defence production estimates, there is no item under which this question concerning the money spent for aircraft engines could be asked. If you look at the defence production estimates on page 12 you will find there is no particular item to which that particular question is relevant. I would imagine that even with a generous chairman such as you have been, if I may say so, you would be bound to rule the hon. gentleman out of order because

there would be no item in these estimates on which he could ask his question. It seems to me the sensible thing to do is have both ministers here, and if one cannot answer the question then the other should.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: One cannot answer and the other will not.

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: As the minister charged with responsibility, I shall be pleased to bring in that information when my estimates come down, if they come down. I suppose that will depend on the length of the session.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I thought the minister was always an optimist.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Order.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I note that the item for clothing and personal equipment is reduced from $31 million last year to $15 million this year. Will the minister comment on that matter?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes; I should be glad to. That is owing to the fact that in 1951, as I announced on February 5, we entered a period of stockpiling equipment for the purposes of mobilization. We also had to replace stocks that were used to equip the forces as they were rapidly built up. Therefore during 1952-53 we spent much larger sums on clothing than were necessary for a normal year. Having replenished our stocks that were necessary to equip the forces and provide something for stockpiling, it is now possible to reduce the amount sought for clothing.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Have any changes been introduced in the style of uniforms for the air force within the last couple of years? For instance, I have been told that last year before one issue was completed the style had been changed and a new style of uniform was introduced.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No, that is not so.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: How many changes of style have been introduced within the last year or two?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The only change of any significance at all that occurs to me as having been made during the last three years is that there is a new working dress for air crew and ground crew along the lines of battle dress.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
To revert again to civil staff, there are a couple of questions I should like to ask. I notice that the department apparently employs one meteorologist. Since ordinarily these men are employed by the Department of Transport, perhaps the minister would explain this one exception and tell us how it comes about that he is employed by the Department of National
Supply-National Defence Defence. Then as a second question I would ask this. I notice that the estimate for payment of the corps of commissionaires has increased considerably, namely by about $150,000. Does this mean that there is an increasing program in effect for replacing service guards by commissionaires for guard duties? Is that the explanation of the increase?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: On the first point, may I say that I am informed that we have one meteorologist attached to air force headquarters, on loan or seconded from the Department of Transport. He is there as an adviser to co-ordinate civilian and air force meteorological activities, and we pay his salary. On the second point, my answer is that the general policy is to reduce the number of service guards to the minimum and to have the corps of commissionaires wherever we can. I might also say that there are 19 new units this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Further on there is an item for the purchase of real properties, land and buildings. There is an increase there of about $5 million. Can the minister explain that increase?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes. This is largely for the purpose of a new air weapons range at Cold Lake, Alberta. That accounts for a great proportion of the increase.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: In connection with the purchase of land at Cold Lake, can the minister tell the committee how the value of this land was arrived at? Was it bought by tender, by some independent arbitration to set the value, or from whom was it bought?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I am informed that this matter was gone into in great detail in the defence expenditure committee where actual unit costs, the procedures and so on were explained.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Shall we pass on to defence research and development?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
No, Mr. Chairman. There is an item here which I was rather surprised to see, namely "gasoline, fuel oil and lubricants for aircraft and mechanical equipment". Last year the amount was $17 million; this year it is about $13,700,000. There is a considerable decrease in spite of what the minister has told us about the increasing activities of the R.C.A.F. and the increasing numbers of aircraft. I found it difficult to understand why the cost of gasoline and lubricants for these aircraft had come down so much.

Supply-National Defence

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The entire reason is, I am told, that the estimate that was made last year was higher than it proved to be necessary.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Can the minister tell us how much actually was expended last year on this particular item?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Of course the figures for the year are not complete yet, but I am informed that the figure of expenditure will be approximately $13 million.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The estimate for this year is being made the same as the amount actually expended last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I suppose the minister
actually expects there will be considerably more flying this year than there was last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: About the same.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: About the same?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes. There will be some increase because we will have two more training stations in operation.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I would think there would be bound to be more flying this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: There is an item for ammunition and bombs which is about half a million dollars more this year than it was last year, being $10,900,000 as against $11,500,000. That is quite a different situation than we had in the navy and in the army, particularly in the army where there was a large increase with regard to ammunition and bombs. So far as the air force goes, can the minister explain why the estimate is approximately the same? The air force is supposedly our chief defensive arm, or the arm upon which we are placing the most emphasis. Why is the estimate approximately the same as last year, and why is it a much smaller amount than is shown in the case of the army and the navy?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: It is owing to the fact that the air force operation does not involve the use of highly expensive rounds as does that of the army and the navy. As to the air force, it is largely small calibre ammunition used in practice. It is only toward the end of the year that we shall be coming into the rocket field in any considerable way.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
What this means particularly, I presume, is that the air force used a comparatively small amount of ammunition last year and it is anticipated that they will


use a small amount this year in comparison with the other two services.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: They will use a great number of rounds but each round costs much less, on the average, than a round in the navy or the army.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: A few moments ago the minister referred to two Comets. Are these the de Havilland jet air liners which we were to obtain in the United Kingdom?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Are they now in the possession of the R.C.A.F.?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes. They have been handed over in the United Kingdom and are now engaged in familiarization flights over routes that have been flown previously with Comets so that the experience can be passed on to our pilots who are being trained to use them, and also so that the aircraft can be tested out over the same flights and results arrived at concerning fuel consiimption, load-carrying capacity and so on.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: How much do these air liners cost apiece?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: They cost something more than $1J million each.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I suppose the idea is to bring them to Canada once they have been tested.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: To what use will they be put here?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Very largely for the purpose of training the fighter defence and the radar coverage, so the fighter defence and the radar stations can be trained on high speed, high altitude aircraft of the most modern type known.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The cabinet are not going to the coronation in them?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Are they to be used for transport purposes as well?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Not so far as I know.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Were they bought by the Minister of Defence Production?

speakerposition: Minister of Defence Production; Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Yes.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Shall we pass on to the next heading?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
Before we pass from the air force estimates may I ask the minister whether it is expected that the air force will be so extended that further training schools will be needed? If so, where is it expected

that these air training schools will be built or reopened? The minister knows that in the past there have been quite a number of air training schools in southern Alberta. Just as soon as some little activity takes place in some of these localities people come to me and ask whether this or that school is to be reopened. Rumours get around.
I think I asked the minister a similar question a little while ago. I have particular reference to the air training school at Vulcan, Alberta and the one at Macleod, two schools that were quite active during the war. They are now almost closed and partially dismantled, but the one at Claresholm has been opened and is, I understand, doing very good work. Is it expected that the air force will be expanded to such an extent that it will require the reopening of any of these other schools?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: We do not expect to be opening any additional schools. The one at Moose Jaw and the one at Penhold will be opened next month, I understand, and that will complete the requirement to meet our estimated need.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I have a couple of questions that are somewhat related to the last one. The first is this. Are some of the schools that have been functioning at full capacity being closed down in the near future? I have in mind especially two air navigation schools. Will both of these continue to function, as well as the central navigation school?
My second question relates to buildings on stations which are now open. From time to time new buildings are erected on certain stations, of necessity, and I was wondering whether there are some stations where buildings of a permanent nature are erected that were opened during the war, and are there other stations where only temporary buildings are erected with the idea that these second-class stations are on a temporary basis and might be closed down at any time? Is there any division along that line as to possible permanency of stations which are now functioning, and which were built during the war as temporary establishment stations?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
The only change which I think the hon. member's question refers to is the transfer of the navigation school from Sum-merside to Winnipeg. That is being done for the purpose of bringing together two schools, because we can meet the needs of both at Winnipeg. The need for training navigators is being met progressively, and we can handle the job both for ourselves and for the NATO countries at Winnipeg. However, the air station at Summerside will continue to be operated on at least its present level through the transfer of the operational training unit
Supply-National Defence for maritime reconnaissance from Greenwood to Summerside, so the facilities at Summer-side will be fully used.
With regard to the second question, wherever it is possible we renovate old buildings, where that is profitable. Where it is not profitable, then if we need a building we replace it with either a class I or II or a class III building.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: With regard to the reconnaissance maritime squadron, a coastal type of squadron, what action is being taken, if any, that the minister might explain to the committee with regard to replacing their present Lancaster aircraft?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I did mention that the other night. These Lancasters are converted for this purpose because there was no aircraft particularly suited for this purpose in this or any other country. To meet our needs the Lancaster as converted was the most suitable aircraft. Of course they will be gradually used up and worn out, and we are looking around for a new type of aircraft to replace the Lancaster. So far we have made no decision about it. That replacement will begin about 1956 or 1957.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Shall we pass on to defence research and development?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I should like to ask the minister some questions concerning the northwest staging operations. When we compare the estimates for the current year with the estimates of last year there seems to be a changeover in the nature of the work, or a change in the emphasis on the nature of the operations on the northwest staging route. There appear to be a number of reductions in some items which are not in keeping with the increases in other items for the northwest staging route.
For example, in pay and allowances for military personnel there has been a reduction of approximately 20 per cent when compared with last year. There also appears to be a substantial reduction in the number of civilian personnel engaged in that operation. There is an increase of about 75 per cent in the appropriation for gasoline, fuel oil and lubricants, which would appear to indicate some substantial increase in the operation of aircraft, on the northwest staging route. At the same time there is a reduction in the item under fuel for heating, cooking and power generating units. There is an increase of 375 per cent in the item for the acquisition and construction of buildings and works.
Then getting down to the smaller items I see that three for which there was provision last year are eliminated from the list this

Supply-National Defence year. There is another small item of postage with whioh, presumably, typists and stenographers would have some connection. I notice that the item for postage is increased to the extent of 150 per cent.
Would the minister give us some explanation of the nature of the operation of the northwest staging route this year as compared with last year, as to why in some instances there are increases and in others decreases, which do not appear quite consistent.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The hon. member is correct in his assumption that there has been a considerable change in the functioning of the northwest staging route. Owing to the increase in the range of the aircraft flying from Edmonton to Alaska, the operations of the various stations on the route have been substantially reduced. There is a consequential reduction in staff and activities. They are being maintained at the lowest possible figure to keep the route open. Then the amount for postage was increased because the amount set aside last year was quite inadequate. As I have said, the other operations have been reduced.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Would the minister explain the item of $705,000 for the acquisition and construction of buildings and works. This, as I have said, represents an increase of about 375 per cent over last year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: This is entirely accounted for by an addition at Whitehorse, valued at $565,000, for the mechanical engineering section, including a drill hall, renovation of and putting cubicles in the barracks block, some work carried over in connection with the storage building and barracks block, and some other items.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I see here an item of $1,090,000 for fuel for heating, cooking and power generating units. This represents about a sixth of the total amount to be voted for the northwest staging route. In view of the high percentage to be voted for fuel, would the minister give us some indication of how fuel costs, which of course would be high in the remote northwest, compare with fuel costs for heating and cooking in other parts of Canada.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: This represents a reduction from last year, when the figure stood at $1,443,520. The reduction this year is due to the reduction to which I referred in my remarks a moment ago. As the hon. member knows, the cost of fuel in that area is very much higher than it is in other parts of Canada. It is very cold there, and a large amount of fuel is used for heating and cooking.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
Before passing the item for search and rescue I should like to take this opportunity to pay tribute to the unit stationed at Torbay, St. John's, Newfoundland. The men of the unit have done and are doing wonderful work not only in mercy flights but in various other activities. This has gone on for some years. The first name that comes to my mind in connection with the original unit is that of Flight Lieutenant Mike Pearson. The present pilot, I believe, is Flight Lieutenant Carl Ensom. Under great difficulties they have evacuated many sick people from various isolated settlements and under trying conditions, at risk of their lives. The last item about which I remember reading was in connection with the recent ice blockade of St. John's harbour, upon which occasion a number of ships were caught in the ice. The search and rescue unit, headed by Flight Lieutenant Carl Ensom, dropped food and other items to the trapped ships.
This gets me down to a further point. They have been greatly assisted in their work by the coastguard service of the United States, stationed at Argentia>. The other evening the hon. member for Comox-Alberni asked the minister about the situation in connection with the setting up of a coastguard service. I do feel that something definite should be done. My recollection is that about a year and a half ago an interdepartmental committee was set up to study the situation and make a report. Whether that report has been made, I cannot say. I was absent from the house for a period of time, and the report may have been made while I was away. However, I do not seem to recollect any decision in the matter.
As the work of search and rescue is being done under this department, I feel it is only proper to urge upon the minister that some decision should be made in connection with the establishment of a coastguard service.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I appreciate the hon. member's remarks about the search and rescue operations, which, I agree, have been admirable. I might point out that the coastguard service concerns a number of government departments. I said a word about it the other evening.
Replying to a question by the hon. member for Calgary East, I would say that the amount spent in the last three years on aircraft and engines has been $682,500,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That figure does not include the $165 million the minister mentioned before?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Can the minister give a breakdown of the $682,500,000?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I have not that information; no.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
Before we leave these
defence items, I believe there are two other questions outstanding which the associate minister was going to answer. One was with reference to the number of deserters, and the other concerned the contract for the removal of ashes at Petawawa.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Solicitor General of Canada
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I have no further information on either point, but the search is still continuing. I will see that the hon. member receives an answer.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: When am I going to get it? If we close out the defence estimates now I am sure I will not have an opportunity to get these answers.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Oh, yes.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: We still have several items.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The items remaining will go through rapidly, because they concern smaller matters.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I hope you are right.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: The minister says he will produce the information, but if we pass all the national defence items I will have no opportunity to say anything more.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Solicitor General of Canada
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: It would take some time to check the figures on deserters; and so far as the other matter is concerned, I have not been able to figure out the cubic footage of the pile of ashes to which my hon. friend referred.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: How about my photographs?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I know the minister will need some time with his foot rule to get the figure for the pile of ashes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: We will give you the figures.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: I would suggest that we leave the last of the defence items-

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
-so the minister can answer these questions when he gets the answers. There are also certain other questions which have not been answered.
Mutual aid-

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I should like to ask the minister a question under this general group headed "mutual aid". My question may involve two or three of the headings that we have just passed, but at any rate they all go together. Can the minister tell the house 68108-257
Supply-National Defence the form in which we extend mutual aid? I note from the item before us that we are asked to appropriate $324 million for mutual aid but it is broken down into the usual items of civil salaries and wages, pay and allowances, pensions, other expenditures and so on. Perhaps the minister knows what I am driving at. In what form do we render mutual aid?
When he is answering that question, will he relate what we spend on mutual aid to the last two headings, namely contributions toward the military costs of NATO and defence expenditures by other government departments? Can he give us this picture in an intelligible form?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
I think it is in the white paper at page 33. The figures are given there. When the hon. member refers to items like civil salaries and wages, those are largely in connection with the air training plan where we charge the direct costs to mutual aid. The mutual aid program includes NATO air training plan, radar No. 4 sets, walkie-talkies and so on. These are the heads under which expenditures are made on mutual aid.
With respect to the second part of the hon. member's question, the form of mutual aid is summarized on page 33. It includes transfers of stock of existing equipment and some equipment of world war II that has subsequently been taken into our own stores. Then there are transfers from new production under which are aircraft and engines, radar sets and ammunition. Then there is NATO air crew training, and the total is set forth there. I think I have given the actual items before. They largely consist of world war II equipment for three divisions plus what we have transferred to the Netherlands, Italy and other countries. With respect to new equipment, it includes radar, walkie-talkies, howitzers, ammunition, explosives, Wasp engines, communications materials, propellants and so on. The program for 1953-54 will in addition include some ships.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext: Then am I correct in my understanding that what we spend on mutual aid is spent either here in Canada or by procurements made by Canada in the usual way? We spend it on hiring technical aid, buying equipment and so on and then we either turn that equipment over to our partners or we make it available to the common pool. Is that a correct statement?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE
speechtext:
The procedure under which we do it is that we arrive at a figure which we propose to give by way of mutual aid and we ask parliament to vote it. Parliament votes it. Before that is done we have made

Supply-National Defence up a catalogue of things that we think the other countries need and that we can provide. As soon as parliament authorizes the vote we offer specific items of equipment to the standing group at Washington. The standing group notifies the North Atlantic treaty nations about them. They bid for them; they ask for them if they want them. The standing group arrives at an appraisal, judgment or recommendation as to which country should get the equipment. It makes that recommendation to us. We usually act on it. Then the cabinet approves the allocation of the equipment and it is shipped at once.
In the case of some equipment which countries like Britain, for example, happen to need particularly, they may make a direct approach to us but we still go through the form of telling the standing group about it and getting their approval in each case. That occurred in the case of aircraft, some propellants and other things. The only item of dollars that has so far entered into this has been that where we agree to pay towards infrastructure a larger proportion than that arrived at on the basis of capacity to pay as judged by national income, we then charge the excess over what we think is the right proportion on the capacity to pay basis to mutual aid. That accounts for probably two or three million dollars.

The first relates to the provision of transportation for the dependents of service personnel in England and Europe. We had hoped that by the principle of rotation it might be possible to rotate married personnel so they would only be separated from their wives and children for a year. Despite that, however, a number have taken their wives and children overseas without government assistance, and it is now proposed that regulations shall be introduced under which the ordinary rules regarding postings shall be applied if the commanding officer of the unit is satisfied that a service officer or man has secured proper accommodation for his wife and family. Transportation will be paid and they will be treated as married persons abroad on the condition that the posting is for a minimum of two years. This will be of major importance to the welfare of our troops abroad.
The second change which was just authorized by the cabinet yesterday is a change in the arrangements regarding subsistence under which the amount payable for subsistence to married personnel in the armed forces is increased substantially. This was done also to meet the condition that has arisen in consequence of having these large peacetime forces with frequent postings, some of them abroad, and the fact that we have not yet been able to provide everyone who wants them with married quarters. Mr. Chairman, in previous
